card: This pull request stores multipath descriptor relationships in the wallet database and reports the reconstructed multipath descriptor string in listdescriptors and watch-only exports. Currently, Bitcoin Core expands multipath descriptors on import and discards their relationship, preventing users from retrieving the original multipath descriptor needed for hardware signer policy registration. By saving relative ScriptPubKeyMan IDs in WalletDescriptor records, the wallet can reconstruct and export the original multipath strings. It depends on #36442 and #36443.
changed_since_previous: No substantial conceptual changes; the PR was rebased on updated prerequisite commits in the multipath descriptor stack.
evidence: PR description: 'This is useful for working with hardware wallets that require policy registration, particularly those that require resending the descriptor that was registered.'
problem: When multipath descriptors are imported or generated, Bitcoin Core expands them into separate internal and external descriptors and stores them independently without recording their relationship. Users interacting with hardware signers that require policy registration cannot retrieve or export the original registered multipath descriptor string from the wallet.

risk.why: Mistakes in wallet descriptor serialization or multipath association logic could corrupt wallet database records or lead to incorrect address derivation and missing funds.

scope_notes: This PR includes commits from prerequisite PRs #36442 (representing multipath descriptors in Descriptor objects and BIP32 KeyPath refactors) and #36443 (multipath reconstruction). The actual wallet changes make up a smaller subset of the overall diff.
summary: Stores multipath descriptor relationships in the wallet database for imported and automatically generated descriptors. Persists the sibling ScriptPubKeyMan IDs in `WalletDescriptor` so that the wallet can reconstruct the original multipath descriptor using `ReconstructMultipath`. Exposes the reconstructed string through an optional `multipath_descriptor` field in `listdescriptors` and includes it in `exportwatchonly` outputs.
